steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: A bitmap image is made up of a grid of small squares called pixels (picture elements). Each pixel is assigned a binary value that represents its colour. | Definition: Resolution is the number of pixels in an image, expressed as width x height. For example, 1920 x 1080 means 1920 pixels across and 1080 pixels down. | Definition: Colour depth (also called bit depth) is the number of bits used to represent the colour of each pixel. More bits per pixel means more possible colours. | Important: There is always a trade-off between file size and image quality. Higher resolution and greater colour depth produce better images but require more storage space and bandwidth.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: An image has a resolution of 1920 x 1080 and a colour depth of 24 bits. Calculate the file size in megabytes. | What is the effect on file size if you double the width of an image but keep the height and colour depth the same? | An image uses 8-bit colour depth. How many different colours can it represent?
